testEnvironment:
Test environment: the snapshot is a git repository whose single commit holds
the reviewed tree — its tree hash was compared against the commit under review
when the snapshot was cut. A suite run here collects and runs what a checkout at
that commit does, so a failing or skipped test is a fact about the tree, not
about this copy of it. Its history is that one synthetic commit: 'git log',
'git diff' and every ancestry question answer about the snapshot and never about
the PR.
The Recipe's Test entrypoint and Check step do not run these merge-gating CI steps, and nothing in this review ran them: rebase-check job (pull_request-only branch-currency assertion, not meaningful in a worktree of origin/main); proc-macos job (node --test tests/proc.test.mjs on macOS) (subsumed by the full suite on this macOS host); smoke-omp job (needs pinned omp installed via bun, absent here); install-and-smoke job (needs pinned omp installed via bun and network, absent here).

survived.claim: commitClosingIssues splices headline and body with a newline, but gh cuts long commit subjects at 69 chars + '…' and starts messageBody with '…'. A subject-line keyword that crosses the cut is missed, or picks up the wrong issue number: '…, closes #3637' scans as [] or as #363.
survived.evidence: Real gh on this PR: `gh pr view 4398 --json commits` printed messageHeadline "fix: read commit messages' closing keywords in the settle and the fin…" (70 chars) and messageBody starting "…isher gate". `gh api .../commits/8ca2b531` printed the full subject on one line. In the copy, node -e commitClosingIssues([{oid:'abc1234', messageHeadline:subj.slice(0,69)+'…', messageBody:'…'+subj.slice(69)}]): subj 'feat: tighten the readers of the settle and the finisher gate, closes #3637' gave `scan []`, and subj '…finisher, closes #3637 x' gave `scan2 [{"number":363,"oid":"abc1234"}]`.
survived.suggested_fix: When messageHeadline ends with '…' and messageBody starts with '…', join them as headline.slice(0,-1)+body.slice(1) before splitting into lines. Add a test with a truncated-headline commit.

survived.claim: COMMIT_SLOSE does not accept a colon after the keyword. GitHub documents that `Closes: #10` and `CLOSES: #10` close the issue, including from a commit message. So a commit saying `Fixes: #K` with #K in-progress passes the settle and the gate, and it still closes #K at merge, stranding the claim. The new closing-refs test also pins `closes: #5` as closing nothing.
survived.evidence: curl of github/docs linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue.md line 57: "The keywords can be followed by colons or in uppercase. For example: `Closes: #10`, `CLOSES #10`, or `CLOSES: #10`." Line 61: commit-message keywords close the issue on merge to the default branch. In the copy, the PROBE settle test with commits [commit(..., 'the work', 'Closes: #7')] and issue 7 labelled in-progress printed `PROBE colon outcome PR#6 []`: it settled and read no issue. The PROBE dispatch test with 'Closes: #3637' and #3637 in-progress printed `status 0`: the finisher was dispatched. node -e: 'Closes: #7' and 'FIXES: #7' both scan to [].
survived.suggested_fix: Allow an optional ':' between the keyword and '#N', e.g. `(?:close[sd]?|fix(?:e[sd])?|resolve[sd]?):?[ \t\r\v\f]*#([0-9]+)`, and move 'closes: #5' from the closes-nothing list to the positive cases. drop-merged-label.sh has the same gap, but the ticket puts changing it out of scope.

survived.claim: Every commit-borne number that is not the PR's own ticket is read with `gh issue view`. A commit that names a number with no issue or PR behind it (a typo, an upstream number in a cherry-pick, `fix #0`) makes both the settle and the gate exit 2 'could not look'. That is the transient code, and run-team says to re-run it once gh answers, but gh never will, so this blocks forever instead of giving a refusal the implementer could act on.
survived.evidence: Real gh: `gh issue view 999999 -R feigi/fleet-plugin --json labels` printed 'GraphQL: Could not resolve to an issue or pull request with the number of 999999.' and exit=1. Same for 0. A PR number (4398) answered exit 0. node -e: commitClosingIssues on 'closes #0' gives [{number:0}]. Copy PROBE (settle, stub dies on a missing issue file): commit 'fixes #99999 upstream' gave f.refused('impl-5', 2, /could not read issue #99999's labels/), which passed. Copy PROBE2 (dispatch, failsOn issue 99999) printed `status 2 stderr ledger: dispatch finisher-pr-3606: could not look — gh issue view 99999 --json title,labels exited 1 ...; nothing written dispatched []`. SKILL.md:822 says an exit 2 that could not look "is run again once gh and git answer".
survived.suggested_fix: Treat gh's 'Could not resolve to an issue or pull request' answer for a commit-borne number as 'no issue, so GitHub closes nothing', or report it as a refusal (exit 3 / gate failure line) naming the commit. Keep the exit-2 death for transient failures only. Add a test for a commit naming a nonexistent issue.

survived.claim: The test "it names what drop-merged-label.sh's commit scan names" pipes through `rtk grep -Eo` inside a `sh -c` and never checks the spawn's status or stderr. Without `rtk` on PATH it fails with a misleading mismatch assertion instead of naming the missing tool, and the repo's CI never installs rtk.
survived.evidence: Ran in my copy with PATH limited to symlinks for node, sh, grep, printf and cat, plus /usr/bin:/bin: `node --test --test-name-pattern='drop-merged-label' tests/closing-refs.test.mjs`. Result: `✖ it names what drop-merged-label.sh's commit scan names` with `AssertionError: "Closes #1" actual [1] expected []`. The real cause, `rtk: not found` on the shell side, is never shown, because `r.status` and `r.stderr` are ignored and `fromShell` just becomes []. `grep -rn rtk .github` in the copy matched nothing, so CI has no rtk. Matches elsewhere are only tests/member-record*.test.mjs, plugin/scripts/member-record.mjs and this test. The full suite passed on the author's host, where /opt/homebrew/bin/rtk exists.
survived.suggested_fix: Use plain `grep -Eo '[0-9]+'` in the pipeline. Assert `r.status === 0 || r.status === 1` (grep's no-match status) and an empty stderr, so a broken shell side fails with its own message.

unverified.claim: The same three-step block appears at both call sites, and prCommitClosing is used nowhere else. The block is: read the commit closes, drop the numbers the body already closes, run claimedElsewhere, then map the result back to commits. It is at closingRefusals (2258-2260) and in the settle path (3011-3013, where `held` is renamed `heldByCommit`). It can be one checkReaders helper.
unverified.evidence: In the copy I added `commitsClaimedElsewhere(pr, judged, own, labelsOf)` to checkReaders, returned it in place of prCommitClosing, and replaced both blocks with `for (const c of commitsClaimedElsewhere(pr, refs, ownTickets, (m) => issueRead(m).labels))` and `for (const c of commitsClaimedElsewhere(report.pr, numbers, [live.number], issueLabels))`. Result: `node --test tests/closing-refs.test.mjs tests/ledger-dispatch.test.mjs tests/ledger-settle-report.test.mjs` → ℹ tests 258, ℹ pass 258, ℹ fail 0. To show those tests reach both sites, I made the helper `return []` and ran `--test-name-pattern='[Cc]ommit'`: 6 of 16 failed, including 'a commit closing a ticket another claim holds refuses the finisher…' (dispatch) and 'impl-N=PR#M: a commit closing a ticket whose issue carries in-progress…' (settle).
unverified.suggested_fix: In checkReaders: `const commitsClaimedElsewhere = (pr, judged, own, labelsOf) => { const byCommit = prCommitClosing(pr).filter((c) => !judged.includes(c.number)); const held = claimedElsewhere(byCommit.map((c) => c.number), own, labelsOf); return byCommit.filter((c) => held.includes(c.number)); };`. Return it from checkReaders in place of prCommitClosing. Both call sites then become `for (const c of commitsClaimedElsewhere(...)) { failures.push(…) / check(…, false) }`.

unverified.claim:
In commitClosingIssues, splitting the message into lines does nothing: the matches are the same whether you split or not. The joined message can go straight to matchAll. COMMIT_CLOSE's gap class `[ 	\v ]*` already excludes 
, so no match crosses a line. Each 
 is itself a `[^\p{L}\p{N}_]` lead character, and a match always ends in a digit, so the 
 is never already used up. That makes a match at the start of a line identical to the `^` case after a split.

Fuzz in the copy (node …/simplify/probe.mjs): commitClosingIssues compared with the same loop using `${headline}
${body}`.matchAll(COMMIT_CLOSE) and no split, over 300000 random 1-3 commit lists. The inputs were built from keywords, #N, digits, _, 
, , 
, 	,  , é,  , a null body and a 20-digit #N. Output: `split-vs-joined trials 300000 diffs 0`. With that edit applied, tests/closing-refs.test.mjs passed 13/13, including its 'closes
#5' and drop-merged-label.sh parity cases.
unverified.suggested_fix: `for (const m of `${c.messageHeadline}\n${body}`.matchAll(COMMIT_CLOSE)) { const number = Number(m[1]); if (Number.isSafeInteger(number) && !first.has(number)) first.set(number, c.oid); }`. To keep the 'per line' framing for readers, add a one-line comment saying the gap class excludes \n.
